title: Tourist Season, 2013
logline: The motel full. A guest at 2 AM asks if the night clerk knows the strip is drawn here. Wood says he's heard that. The guest has the Sunday on his phone; Wood looks at his own bay on a screen for the first time.

panels.composition: The desk, 2 AM. A GUEST, phone out, showing WOOD a Sunday — the January Rain. The hum line.

balloons.text: This is here, right? The guy's from here?

image.prompt: a motel night desk at 2 AM with a guest holding out a phone showing a watercolor comic page to a clerk in a maroon polo, a flat unbroken line running beneath the panel

panels.composition: The phone. The bay, wet-on-wet, glowing on the screen. Smaller than a hand. Brighter than the paper ever was.

image.prompt: close-up of a phone screen glowing with a small bright watercolor of a bay in rain
image.notes: The first time the strip draws itself on a screen. It looks better and smaller.

panels.composition: Wood looking at it a beat too long. The guest noticing.

image.prompt: a clerk looking at a guest's phone a beat too long while the guest watches him

panels.composition: The guest gone up. The desk. The door. Beyond it, the lot, the highway, and twelve blocks off, unseen, the bay, which is not bright. The hum line.

image.prompt: a motel desk at night with a clerk alone, the glass door onto a dark lot and highway, a flat unbroken line running beneath the panel, no words

art.line: razor-sharp, confident brush and ink; pristine perspective; crisp silhouettes; zero crosshatch in close-ups
art.palette: dailies: black ink, one spot tone at most. Sundays: wet-on-wet — gray-green moss, fog, rusted tin, bruised dusk
art.paper: bristol for dailies; 140 lb Arches cold-press for Sundays
